title: Circular Game (Josephus Problem)
statement_html:
There are n people standing in a circle, numbered 0 to n - 1. Starting from person 0, every k-th person is eliminated (counting the current person as 1). After each elimination, counting resumes from the next person. This continues until only one person remains.

Return the position (0-indexed) of the survivor.

Input: one line with two integers n and k.

Output: a single integer: the 0-indexed position of the survivor.

Example 1:

Input: 5 2
Output: 2
Explanation: People are eliminated in the order 1, 3, 0, 4; person 2 survives.

Example 2:

Input: 6 5
Output: 0

Example 3:

Input: 1 1
Output: 0

Example 4:

Input: 7 3
Output: 3

Example 5:

Input: 41 3
Output: 30

Constraints:

  • 1 <= n <= 107

  • 1 <= k <= 107

Note: the limits are intentionally large. A naive O(n·k) queue simulation will time out; use the mathematical recurrence instead.

Same game as LeetCode #1823. Find the Winner of the Circular Game: there people are numbered from 1 (so its answer is this one + 1) and n <= 500; here n, k go up to 107, so the O(n) recurrence (LeetCode's follow-up) is required.
